newsitem.title: USA: NY/NJ Port Authority chief Marlin to step down.
newsitem.headline: NY/NJ Port Authority chief Marlin to step down.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said Friday executive director George Marlin will step down from his post.

According to a spokesman for the authority, Marlin has notified Gov Christine Whitman of New Jersey and Gov George Pataki of New York that he will not seek a third one-year term when his current term expires April 3. Marlin was appointed to the post in 1995.
In letters to Whitman and Pataki, Marlin said he has decided to return to the private sector.
He cited among his accomplishments at the helm of the authority eliminating 1,300 positions, or 15 percent, of the agency's staff, and cutting its operating budget for the first time since 1943.
Marlin said he was able to avoid toll and fare increases, and privatized the Vista Hotel and industrial parks in Yonkers and Elizabeth.

Marlin, a conservative party candidate for New York City mayor, became a controversial appointee to the authority after Gov Whitman's administration complained Pataki floated Marlin's name without first consulting her. Other critics assailed Marlin's lack of experience in the public sector.
